newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Modest rise despite crude surge.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Modest rise despite crude surge.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps rose by about half the increase seen on overnight crude values at midday on Tuesday as bearish regional fundamentals tampered the rise, traders said.
"The market took the cue from crude and prices rose but the increase was small becuase product prices here are already quite high," one trader said.

Gas oil swaps, the most actively traded oil derivative product in Asia, rose by about 50 cents after June Brent closed 79 cents higher to $19.72 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange on Monday.
June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.45/$25.55 per barrel up from Monday's $25.00/$25.10, brokers said.
June traded earlier in the day $25.50 and $25.55 before easing slightly at midday.
July swaps also rose to last quote at $25.10/$25.20 from Monday's $24.65/$24.75. It traded earlier at $25.18 and $25.20, brokers said.

Traders said the market remains uncertain over the future direction as physical trading over the past two weeks and were range bound at between $25.00 and $25.50 per barrel on a free-on-board basis as neither buyers nor sellers were keen to
push the market forcefully in any direction.

The jet fuel market also rose with the regrade remaining unchanged despite the firmer gas oil prices. Brokers said June jet was traded at $25.71 and $25.72 with a US major selling to a European refiner.
The traded levels equated to an unchanged regrade value of about 10-30 cents, they said.

Fuel oil swaps rise slightly in quiet trading with June swaps last quoted at $102.25/$103.25 per tonne, up from Monday's $101.50/$102.50, brokers said. In the morning, bids were at a low of $100.50, they said.
